questions.q: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.
o: a college now
Ms. Malathi is
questions.s:
Answer: old much

Explanation:
The phrase "old much" is grammatically incorrect. The correct form should be "too old" when expressing that someone’s age prevents them from doing something.

Correct sentence:
"Ms. Malathi is too old to join a college now."

Other parts:

  • "Ms. Malathi is" – correct

  • "to join" – correct

  • "a college now" – correct

Hence, "old much" is the part containing the error.

Select the correct superlative degree of comparison for the given sentence.

This is one of the beautiful places in the area.
o: This is one of the most beautiful places in the area.
This is one of the more beautiful places in the area.
This is one of the beautiful places in the area.
This is a beautiful place in the area.
questions.s: (a) Explanation:- ye adjective ki change of degree ka question hai yhan beautiful ki superlative degree likhni hai jo ki most beautiful hoti hai.

questions.q: The flowers in the garden looked vibrantly, brightening up the surroundings.
o: The flowers in the
brightening up the surroundings.
questions.s:
Generally, verbs are modified by adverbs. But verbs of sensation (seem, look, appear, feel, taste, sound, and smell) and ‘be’, ‘become’, ‘turn’, ‘get’, ‘grow’, ‘keep’, ‘make’, and ‘prove’ are followed by an adjective and not an adverb.

According to the given rule, the correct option is (c) "garden looked vibrantly."

So, the error lies in using "vibrantly" as an adverb instead of using the adjective "vibrant" to modify the verb "looked."

The corrected sentence should be: "The flowers in the garden looked vibrant, brightening up the surroundings."

questions.s: Replace ‘early’ with ‘earlier’. Here in the sentence comparison between ‘cashier’ and ‘accountant’ is evident.

questions.q: Even today (1)/ it is incredulous to think (2)/ that men have walked on the moon. /(3) No error. (4)

questions.q: The cake tastes sweetly and moistly, just like homemade.
questions.s:
The correct option is (d) "sweetly and moistly."

So, the error lies in using "sweetly" and "moistly" as adverbs instead of using the adjectives "sweet" and "moist" to modify the verb "tastes."

The correct sentence should be: "The cake tastes sweet and moist, just like homemade."

questions.q: I prefer apples more than oranges.
questions.s:
With the verb prefer, we do not use “more than.”
“Prefer” itself already shows comparison.
So the correct sentence is: I prefer apples to oranges.

o: The river Ganga has some of the most purest water on earth.
The river Ganga has some of the very purest water on earth.
The river Ganga has some of the more purest water on earth.
The river Ganga has some of the purest water on earth.
questions.s:
The correct option that converts the given sentence into the superlative degree is:

The river Ganga has some of the purest water on earth.

"Purest" is the superlative form of "pure," indicating the highest level of purity.

The use of "some of" implies that the Ganga has among the highest purity levels, and the superlative "purest" accurately conveys this meaning.

In summary, the sentence is correctly converted into the superlative degree by using "purest" to emphasize the exceptional purity of the water in the river Ganga.
